| [NOTE-029](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-029.md) | Krauska & Lau 2023, moving away from lexicalism | Standard production and comprehension models built on "lemmas" (stored triads of meaning, syntax and form, with syntax stopping at the word) inherit a lexicalist assumption that typology has refuted. Replacing that assumption needs new algorithms, not just new representations: separate meaning↔syntax and syntax↔form mappings with one integrated stage for retrieving and assembling syntactic structure. This predicts different aphasia profiles. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-052](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-052.md) | Consciousness in AI: indicator properties | Assuming computational functionalism, the report derives a rubric of 14 "indicator properties" from leading neuroscientific theories of consciousness (RPT, GWT, computational HOTs, AST, PP, agency and embodiment). | [NOTE-054](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-054.md) | Brain states across spacetime via whole-brain models | The authors argue that healthy waking brain states sit in a metastable regime between order and disorder. On this view, depression is an overly rigid landscape with dominant attractors and psychedelics flatten the landscape. Whole-brain models, meaning connectome-coupled nonlinear oscillators near a Hopf bifurcation, are the mechanistic tool for explaining these spatiotemporal signatures and for finding perturbations that move between states. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-067](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-067.md) | The sound of an axon's growth | The authors propose that an axon can regulate its length by reading the spectral composition, rather than the frequency, of motor-generated oscillating signals whose period grows with length. Coupling that signal to growth-cone extension and actin contraction produces a stable length. In some parameter regions fewer motors make axons longer, as experiments show. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-075](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-075.md) | Surface optimization in physical networks | The local branching of real physical networks (neurons, vasculature, trees, corals, plants) is predicted by minimizing surface area under a minimum-thickness constraint, not wire length. That explains the observed trifurcations, non-planar and asymmetric branch angles, and orthogonal sprouts, which Steiner and volume minimization forbid. | Skimmed |
